explanation: States the p ≥ 3 version, which erdosproblems.com/273 reports Selfridge solved (an example with moduli dividing 360): there is a covering system with distinct moduli all of the form p - 1 for primes p ≥ 3. Unlike the main theorem it uses StrictCoveringSystem ℕ rather than ℤ, where cosets are r + mℕ. Existence is equivalent, since a ℤ-covering with residues reduced below the moduli restricts to an ℕ-covering, and conversely. The inconsistency is cosmetic.
